title: Bending Nail Hammer
normalExpectation: Hammering a nail drives it straight into wall.
response: Every hammer strike causes the nail to bend away from the wall at a right angle; bending increases with force.
whyThisObject: Hammer is meant to apply axial force to nail; if nail deflects under any force, it cannot penetrate.
trigger: Kiko hits nail; it curves 90 degrees without entering wall.
goalInterference: The action to hang frame fails as nail never goes straight, preventing secure mounting.
frameZero: Kiko holds hammer mid-swing, but the nail protruding from the wall is bent into a U-shape, and the picture frame leans beside him.

evidenceRefs.sourceText: Hammer
Hammering a nail drives it straight into wall.
Every hammer strike causes the nail to bend away from the wall at a right angle; bending increases with force.
Hammer is meant to apply axial force to nail; if nail deflects under any force, it cannot penetrate.
The nail bends around the pliers and grips them, trapping the tool.
The long nail curls into a spiral, then springs back and pings off the wall.
The nail passes halfway, then bends sideways and splits the wallboard, making a large hole.
The hammer leaps from his hand, straightens the bent nail with one tap, then hammers it perfectly into the wall.
All nails in the room curve, pictures crash, and the original nail pings into Kiko's hand, bending his thumb comically.

sourceBeats.visibleConsequence: The long nail curls into a spiral, then springs back and pings off the wall.
sourceBeats.newInformation: Nail length increases elasticity, causing projectile bending.

sourceBeats.strategy: Kiko pre-drills a hole, then taps the nail.
sourceBeats.visibleConsequence: The nail passes halfway, then bends sideways and splits the wallboard, making a large hole.
sourceBeats.newInformation: The nail bends at a specific depth, damaging the wall.

sourceBeats.strategy: Kiko grabs the hammer to adjust the picture, but the hammer now bends every nail in the house.
